note: Ready-to-add effects. Each entry is a BEAT (or layer) in the engine's own grammar with its variable parts named in `params`. `scripts/add-effect.mjs` stamps one into a reel.json; nothing here is new engine code - every effect is an existing primitive, so a reel using them renders on any engine that has that primitive. Replicated from the owner's reference edit (25 Oct): a podcast breakdown whose effects map one-to-one onto kinds the engine already builds.

word-tiles.what: A text page on grid paper: a small kicker, a big headline, a serif line under it. The reference's stacked word tiles.
word-tiles.note: Hand-written collage items need explicit x/y - the auto-stack only runs on the paper->collage path, so items with no position all land at 120,600 on top of each other.

keyword-takeover.what: One huge serif word over dimmed, blurred footage. The reference's big coloured keyword.
keyword-takeover.note: `size` auto-fits the width, so a long word shrinks rather than running off frame. 2-3 words reads best.

ring-badge.what: A glass ring badge with a number, which shrinks into a row with its label typed beside it. The reference's percentage ring.
ring-badge.note: `label` takes **bold part** markup. `labelAt` is when the badge shrinks and the label types in.
ring-badge.needs: nothing: a number and a label
ring-badge.cannot: the badge is a full glass CIRCLE. A partial progress ARC, like the reference's red 32% arc, does not exist.

box-words.what: Lines inking in word by word, one of them growing an accent box under the words as they land. The reference's highlighted box words.
box-words.note: Every line's words must be SPOKEN while the page is up or the build warns that it will lag the voice.
box-words.needs: nothing, but every line must be words SPOKEN while it is up

card-word.what: A word on a navy card in condensed serif caps. The reference's word on black.
card-word.note: This kind takes `lines`, NOT `text`. A `text` field builds an empty card with no warning.

text-behind.what: Two to four big words BEHIND the speaker, their head and shoulders cutting the letters.
text-behind.needs: reel.matte - the speaker is cut out. ~26 min per 10 s of footage on this CPU, so matteWindows + matteClip keep it to the seconds that need it
text-behind.cannot: no outline around the cut-out: the .matte class takes a CSS filter but no beat field exposes it.

chrome-overlay.what: A Chrome Motion graphic over live footage instead of replacing the speaker; several can be on screen at once (mac-79).
chrome-overlay.note: A LAYER, not a beat: goes in reel.layers[]. Times are finished-video seconds. All five gm kinds work.

window-grid.what: A 2x2 grid of video windows landing one after another over the footage.
window-grid.note: Four video LAYERS with staggered `at`. Each needs a box; `audio: off` keeps the voice clean.
window-grid.needs: YOUR OWN CLIPS - one video file per window, in assets/
window-grid.cannot: the engine supplies none: four windows need four files.

grey-room.what: The reference's signature frame: the room drops to greyscale with a grid over it and the speaker stays in COLOUR on top, with type beside him.
grey-room.needs: reel.matte - the speaker is cut out, same cost note as text-behind
grey-room.note: `backdrop` is a CSS filter on the room only; the cut-out speaker is drawn over it unfiltered, which is what keeps him in colour.

bw-sentence.what: One sentence drops to black and white, hard cut in and out, like a grade change between shots. The reference's desaturated lines.
bw-sentence.note: Filters the whole picture for the window; there is no per-region version.

limitations: A progress ARC (the reference's red 32%) - `stats` draws a full glass circle only.
Engraved or embossed type (the reference's AUDIENCE caps) - motion text offers shadow soft/strong, no emboss.
An outline around the cut-out speaker - .matte takes a CSS filter, but no field exposes it.
A real UI mockup (a YouTube or Instagram page) needs YOUR screenshot: `ui` draws a synthetic app, `device` frames an image you supply.
A split screen with a second person needs YOUR second clip.
A photo collage needs YOUR photos: collage `image` items read library/engravings, a fixed set.
